abstract: $K$ users share independent GHZ states, each held by a subset of the users, and want a common secret key, using local operations and public classical communication (LOCC). We show that the conference key capacity, the largest number of secret key bits per copy of the resource, equals the key capacity of the classical source obtained by measuring every GHZ state. Measuring first is therefore optimal, even when the users keep quantum memory and communicate over any number of rounds. The capacity also equals the GHZ distillation capacity, the largest number of GHZ states shared by all users obtainable per copy.
